newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stocks steady in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Amman stocks steady in thin volume.

text.p: Jordanian shares closed largely steady on Sunday in thin volume with a lack of institutional demand accompanied by a shortage of supply, dealers said.

The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose a slight 0.06 percent to 166.60 points in 261,667 dinar turnover ($369,064), its lowest volume since April when it hit a fifteen month low.
"The market was very quiet with minimal demand and supply in the absence of institutional demand," said Mohammad Abdullah, senior anaylst at Pearl Consulting.
The busiest traded stock, Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturing, shed 0.04 dinars to 4.12 dinars in 45,218 dinars worth of trade buttressed by investor expectations of healthy half year results.
Heavyweight Arab Bank, which drove the official index up to a three-year high earlier in July, was unchanged at 294 dinars in only 40 share trade.
Local investors piled into the shares in recent weeks, anticipating strong 1997 profits, announcements of a bonus share offering, and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
Overall 19 shares rose on Sunday and 15 fell while nine closed unchanged.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, shed 0.08 percent to 80.90 points, 2.99 percent down since the start of the year. $1 = 0.709 dinars
